            <h3>Timothy hay</h3>
            <p>
              Timothy hay is one of the most popular and widely recommended types of hay for rabbits. It is high in fibre and relatively low in calcium and protein, making it ideal for adult rabbits.
            </p>
            <div class="rch-cuts">
              <div class="rch-cut"><strong>First cut</strong><span>Coarser, stemmier and often contains more seed heads.</span></div>
              <div class="rch-cut"><strong>Second cut</strong><span>Softer, greener and often preferred by rabbits.</span></div>
              <div class="rch-cut"><strong>Third cut</strong><span>Very soft and leafy, but usually slightly lower in fibre.</span></div>
            </div>
          </article>

          <article class="rch-hay-card">
            <div class="rch-hay-icon">🌿</div>
            <h3>Meadow hay</h3>
            <p>
              Meadow hay is made from a mixture of natural grasses and plants. This variety can be especially appealing because it often includes different textures and flavours that rabbits enjoy.
            </p>
            <ul class="rch-mini-list">
              <li>Variety of grasses</li>
              <li>Natural taste</li>
              <li>Good fibre content</li>
              <li>Feels close to natural grazing</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <article class="rch-hay-card">
            <div class="rch-hay-icon">🍃</div>
            <h3>Orchard grass hay</h3>
            <p>
              Orchard grass hay is softer than timothy hay and has a slightly sweet smell. It can be a good alternative for rabbits that are picky eaters or refuse timothy hay.
            </p>
            <ul class="rch-mini-list">
              <li>Soft and leafy</li>
              <li>High in fibre</li>
              <li>Gentle on sensitive noses</li>
              <li>May produce less dust</li>

            <h3>Alfalfa hay</h3>

              <li>Best for baby rabbits</li>
